RagShortTexts: Nahasavi Horse: Aserai desert war horse with excellent endurance and adaptability to the intense heat

Variants.Content: The Nahasawi horse is a kind of war horse common in the Aserai region, named after the Nahasa desert. They are not very tall, but have excellent endurance, a gentle and tough temperament, and can travel in the hot desert for a long time without getting tired. The Aserai's light cavalry mostly fight on such horses, throwing their javelins as they charge and then quickly gaining distance.

Nahasavima is the most trusted companion of our Aserai warriors. They may not have the impact of the armored behemoths of Vlandia, but those expensive horses will fall within three days of arriving in our desert. Our horses know how to save energy on the sand, how to draw strength from the scarce forage, and how to endure the hot sun and windy sand. Riding a good Nahathavi horse, you can close in before your enemies can react, hurl your javelin, and quickly disappear behind the dunes.

Don’t underestimate Nahasavima. The Empire's heavy cavalry was indeed formidable, but their horses were unable to move even an inch on the sand dunes of Nahasa. Riding on such horses, our cavalry can sweep through enemy formations like the wind, disrupt their formations with javelins, and then quickly break away. In the desert, speed and endurance are more important than thick armor.

I am riding the Nahathavi horse. It is not a rare breed, but it has never abandoned me on the battlefield. Once we were chased by the Imperial Legion and ran continuously for a whole day. The other horses were frothing at the mouth and fell down, but my horse was still holding on. When they could no longer pursue us, we turned around and dispersed them with a round of javelin fire. Just because of this, I will never change to another mount in my life.

The Nahathavi horse is the most realistic horse. It is not as expensive as those noble horses, and it is not delicate to feed, but its endurance is really good. Our Aserai caravans rely on this kind of horse to travel long distances. Of course, if you meet a horse thief in the desert, it can carry you and run very fast - and the warrior on horseback will reward the thief with a javelin.

The Nahasavi horse is the war horse of the Aserai people. To be honest, in terms of size and impact, it is far inferior to our imperial war horses; in terms of speed, it is also inferior to those fast horses on the grassland. But its endurance is indeed amazing, and it is very practical in long-distance marches and desert operations. The Aserai cavalry rode it close, threw their javelins and ran away, and our heavy infantry often couldn't catch up. The empire's border guards sometimes acquire some for patrol missions in the south.

When we fought against the Aserai on the southern front, their biggest headache was their javelin cavalry. They rode Nahasavi horses and ran fast and long. They rushed over and threw a javelin, which disrupted our formation. By the time we regrouped and tried to catch up, they were already far away. That kind of horse is at home in the desert.

Nahasavima? That kind of desert pony? On flat ground, our flag knights can knock them away with a single charge. But I also admit that our competitive horses cannot outrun them in a hellish place like the desert. Those Aserai approach on these horses, throw their javelins and run away, never confronting you.

The knights of Vlandia look down upon Nahathavima, but I find this attitude silly. While fighting on the southern shore of the Perath Sea, our horses often fell in droves from the heat and lack of water, while the Aserai rode their horses up and down the dunes, harassing our flanks with their javelins. Whether a horse is good or not depends on where it runs.

Horses in the north are adapted to ice and snow, while horses in the south are adapted to deserts. If Nahasavima reached Sturgia, he would freeze to death in the winter. But then again, if our horses went to Nahasa, they would probably die from the heat. The Creator gave each land a suitable horse.

We Battanians rarely fight on horseback, and horses cannot escape in the forest. However, I have seen the Nahathavi horse ridden by the Aserai merchants. It looks thin, but it is not tired even if it carries heavy goods for a whole day. It is a hard-working animal.

Nahasavima? The endurance is good, but the speed is incomparable with our prairie horses. The Aserai used this kind of horse to harass people, throwing javelins and running away. And our Khuzait mounted archers are particular about running and shooting, flying kites along the way. Everyone has their own way of playing. However, in terms of the explosive power of horses, our grassland horses are stronger.

If you are going to be active in the Aserai area, it is most cost-effective to buy a Nahathavi horse. It’s not expensive, it’s not easy to die, and there are horse dealers everywhere in the desert, so you don’t feel bad if it breaks. If you rode an expensive horse into the desert, just feeding it water and fodder could bankrupt you.
